cause_quote: The introducing diff added `if (!origin?.startsWith("https://")) { return undefined; }` and registered the socket renewal callback only inside `if (identity.signal && !context.handler.isClosed())`, leaving hellos sent while Serve was unpublished with no renewal signal.
user_saw: If the macOS app reconnected during a Tailscale Serve outage, its dashboard stayed on the shared token profile with the default theme and no pinned shortcuts even after Serve recovered, until the app was relaunched.
summary: The Gateway now closes eligible operator sockets when managed Tailscale Serve publishes, so they reconnect and receive a hello with the dashboard sign-in URL.
reasoning: The introducing diff added both the Gateway hello field and the macOS code that reads it from the last hello snapshot. Its route signal covered withdrawal and replacement of a published route, leaving the recovery gap present from the first implementation. First-parent history shows no intervening changes to the identity resolver or the route publication module before this fix.
